subject: social-studies
title: Foundations of High School United States History and Geography
essential_question: How do historians and geographers build defensible claims about the American past?
performance_task: Build a sourcing-and-corroboration casebook that tests one claim about American founding ideals against primary and secondary evidence.
anchor_sources: Declaration of Independence (National Archives)
Constitution of the United States and its amendments (National Archives)
Northwest Ordinance of 1787 (Avalon Project)

subject: social-studies
title: Industrial and Urban America, 1870-1900
essential_question: How did industrial growth reshape where and how Americans lived and worked?
topics: western settlement and federal Indian policy
performance_task: Produce a multi-source causal analysis of how industrial growth reshaped work, cities, and migration, using at least one data set and one firsthand account.
anchor_sources: United States Census reports, 1870-1900 (U.S. Census Bureau)
Dawes Act of 1887 (National Archives)
Detroit Publishing Company photograph collection (Library of Congress)

subject: social-studies
title: Becoming a World Power and World War I
essential_question: Why and how did the United States become a world power, and what did that shift cost?
topics: growth of United States global power
causes of World War I and American entry
the domestic impact of World War I
the Fourteen Points and the peace settlement
performance_task: Write an evidence-based position paper on the League of Nations debate that names and fairly represents at least two period positions.
anchor_sources: Treaty of Versailles, 1919 (Avalon Project)
Congressional Record, League of Nations ratification debate, 1919-1920 (U.S. Government Publishing Office, govinfo.gov, and HathiTrust)
Espionage Act of 1917 and Sedition Act of 1918 (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: The Progressive Era
essential_question: Whose problems did Progressive reform solve, and whose did it leave unsolved?
topics: regulation and the role of government
exclusions and limits of Progressive reform
performance_task: Evaluate the Progressive Era with a claim, a named counterclaim, and an evidence set that addresses both achievements and exclusions.
anchor_sources: Sixteenth, Seventeenth, Eighteenth, and Nineteenth Amendments (National Archives)
Pure Food and Drug Act of 1906 (National Archives)
National American Woman Suffrage Association records (Library of Congress)

subject: social-studies
title: Boom, Depression, and the New Deal
essential_question: What caused the Great Depression, and how far did the New Deal change the role of government?
topics: social and cultural change in the 1920s
the changing role of the federal government
performance_task: Build a data-and-testimony exhibit explaining Depression causes and evaluating New Deal responses with cited evidence.
anchor_sources: Farm Security Administration photograph collection (Library of Congress)
Social Security Act of 1935 (National Archives)
Federal Writers' Project life histories (Library of Congress)

subject: social-studies
title: World War II
essential_question: How did World War II transform the United States at home and abroad?
topics: the geography and course of the war
the Holocaust and the American response
the war's end and atomic weapons
performance_task: Complete a documented inquiry on one wartime decision, weighing context, evidence, alternatives, and consequences.
anchor_sources: Executive Order 9066, 1942 (National Archives)
Korematsu v. United States, 323 U.S. 214 (1944) (Library of Congress)
Report of the Commission on Wartime Relocation and Internment of Civilians, 1982-1983 (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: Cold War and Postwar America
essential_question: How did Cold War commitments abroad reshape American life at home?
topics: the Great Society, Vietnam-era controversies, Watergate, and the environmental movement
performance_task: Create a comparative analysis of two postwar policy decisions, one foreign and one domestic, using primary sources and maps.
anchor_sources: Truman Doctrine address to Congress, 1947 (National Archives)
National Security Act of 1947 (National Archives)
Servicemen's Readjustment Act of 1944, the G.I. Bill (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: Civil Rights in the Post-World War II Era
essential_question: How did legal, legislative, and grassroots strategies interact in movements for rights?
topics: origins of the civil rights movement
performance_task: Analyze how legal, legislative, and grassroots strategies interacted, supporting a defensible interpretation with documents.
anchor_sources: Brown v. Board of Education, 347 U.S. 483 (1954) (National Archives)
Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Voting Rights Act of 1965 (National Archives)
Americans with Disabilities Act of 1990 (National Archives)

subject: social-studies
title: America in a New Global Age
essential_question: How do documented patterns since 1870 inform current policy debates?
topics: globalization and the United States economy
domestic political realignment, religion in politics, and partisanship
America's changing role in the world after the Cold War
performance_task: Complete the course capstone: a researched historical argument connecting one documented pattern since 1870 to a current policy debate.
anchor_sources: Immigration and Nationality Act Amendments of 1965, the Hart-Celler Act (National Archives)
United States Census Bureau population and economic series (census.gov)
Federal Reserve Economic Data series (fred.stlouisfed.org)
